questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has an opposite side of 6 cm and a hypotenuse of 10 cm. Find the angle to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: sin(theta) = O/H = 6/10 = 0.6. theta = sin^(-1)(0.6) = 36.9 degrees (1 d.p.). Writing 0.6 degrees is the error of not using the inverse function.

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has an opposite side of 8 cm and an adjacent side of 6 cm. Find the angle to 1 decimal place.
A right-angled triangle has an adjacent side of 5 cm and a hypotenuse of 13 cm. Find the angle to 1 decimal place.
A wheelchair ramp is 3.5 m long and rises 0.5 m vertically. What angle does the ramp make with the horizontal? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
In a right-angled triangle, the two shorter sides are 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the smallest angle in the triangle to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: The smallest angle is opposite the shortest side (9 cm). Hypotenuse = sqrt(81 + 144) = 15 cm. sin(theta) = 9/15 = 0.6. theta = sin^(-1)(0.6) = 36.9 degrees. The other non-right angle is 90 - 36.9 = 53.1 degrees.
